messages.author: c388c66f81aaadc0
messages.subject: maximum specific stomach energy calculation
parts:
Dear Mike,

We are trying to calculate the stomach energy density for our lizard species, but can't quite figure out how this is done. For example, in

Kearney, M.R., Simpson, S.J., Raubenheimer, D., Kooijman, S.A.L.M., 2013. Balancing heat, water and nutrients under environmental change: a thermodynamic niche framework. Functional Ecology 27, 950–966.

it is mentioned that food has an energy content of 21.525 kJ/g and that stomach volume makes up 13.4% of total body volume, but I can't figure out how this produces the resulting estimate of E_s_m = 1116 J/cm3. Would you mind clarifying how this calculation is done?

Thanks in advance,

Romain Richard.

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: maximum specific stomach energy calculation
parts:
Dear Romain,
It's the maximum energy the stomach can hold per unit of structural volume of the whole organism at a given moment, and its value will therefore depend on your parameter estimates for your species and the energy and water content you give the food. The simplest thing is to play around with the value for E_sm and find one that approximates reality when you look at the model outputs. You could alternatively formally include it in your DEB parameter estimation procedure.
All the best,
Mike
